skill.name: investigating-codebases
skill.description: Investigates unfamiliar codebases by mapping structure, finding entry points, tracing dependencies, and explaining implementation flows with file references.
skill.summary: Builds an evidence-based map of unfamiliar code and explains how components work together.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documentation examples, file discovery, quoted metadata commands, and `/dev/null` redirection. Five `find` substitutions are confirmed because an option-like project argument can be interpreted as `-delete` and remove files. The same flaw affects four earlier `find` pipelines; no prompt injection, network activity, credential access, or exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: The structure script passes an unnormalized project argument to `find`, allowing expression or action injection.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve the argument to an absolute path before any command, reject failures, and use that normalized path for every `find` call.

content.value_statement: Unfamiliar repositories make implementation questions slow and uncertain. This skill maps structure, traces dependencies, and explains behavior with concrete file references.
actual_capabilities: Maps directory structure and identifies common source, test, configuration, and documentation locations.
Finds likely entry points for Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, Java, and web projects.
Traces local TypeScript, JavaScript, and Python imports to a configurable depth.
Follows routes, handlers, services, repositories, and data transformations through related files.
Produces structured explanations with file references, execution flows, patterns, and related components.
limitations: It does not modify code or validate behavior by running the application or its tests.
Import tracing does not resolve aliases, dynamic imports, or every language and build system.
Results depend on the files and repository scope available to the assistant.
The structure script requires a trusted directory argument until its option-injection flaw is fixed.

use_cases.title: Understand a New Repository
use_cases.description: Map the project, identify entry points, and learn the main architectural conventions before making changes.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers joining an existing project

use_cases.title: Trace a Feature
use_cases.description: Follow a feature from its trigger through handlers, services, storage, and response formatting.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Technical Review
use_cases.description: Document component boundaries, dependencies, data flows, and security-sensitive paths with evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Find an Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Find where [feature] is implemented. Name the primary files, explain each role, and include precise file references.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a focused location answer.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how [component] works from entry point to output. Trace important calls and data transformations with file references.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs an implementation walkthrough.

prompt_templates.title: Map Repository Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate this repository architecture. Identify entry points, layers, shared modules, integrations, tests, conventions, and important configuration without reading secret values.
prompt_templates.scenario: A new maintainer needs a broad technical map.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Cross-Cutting Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace [workflow] across modules and services. Document branches, validation, state changes, failure handling, security controls, performance concerns, and unresolved questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced reviewer needs a deep evidence-based analysis.

output: The investigation identifies the request middleware, token validator, session storage, and login handler.
It explains the decision branches and cites each relevant file and line.

output_examples.output: The report traces startup from the main entry point through configuration, dependency initialization, route registration, and server startup.

output_examples.input: Map the payment workflow and its failure paths.
output: The analysis follows request validation, payment service calls, persistence, retries, and error responses.
It separates verified behavior from open questions and lists related components.

best_practices: Start with repository structure and entry points before tracing a specific implementation.
Verify conclusions across definitions, callers, tests, and configuration files.
Separate confirmed behavior from assumptions, and cite a file reference for every important claim.
anti_patterns: Do not search the entire repository without first defining the feature or workflow boundary.
Do not infer runtime behavior from names or directory structure alone.
Do not expose credentials or secret values found in configuration files.

faq.question: Can this skill change the code?
faq.answer: No. Its workflow focuses on reading, searching, tracing, and documenting existing code.

faq.question: Which languages does it support?
faq.answer: The methodology is general, while bundled entry-point clues cover JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, and common web frameworks.

faq.question: Does it run the application or tests?
faq.answer: No. It explains static evidence and does not validate behavior through runtime execution.

faq.question: Can it trace dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It follows imports and related calls, with a helper for local TypeScript, JavaScript, and Python imports.

faq.question: How are findings presented?
faq.answer: Findings include an overview, key files, implementation steps, execution flow, patterns, related components, and concrete file references.

faq.question: Will it read environment secrets?
faq.answer: It may identify configuration locations, but users should limit access and request analysis without exposing secret values.
